_readme: 人工复核记录与修正。手写文件，进 git，PR 里逐条 review。
键是 deckId/cardId。不在这里的牌一律 reviewStatus=unreviewed。
replace: 逐字精确子串替换，作用于 scene 与全部列表条目（推荐，跨重新生成仍然有效）
patch:   整字段覆盖（会连带盖掉该字段里模型写的其它条目，慎用）
uncertainFields: 人工判定不可靠的字段，整个清空、不进 Reading Prompt
reason / reviewer / reviewedAt 只进 QA 报告，绝不进 Reading Prompt。
用 npm run visual:review 查看与标记；改完跑 npm run visual:check 验证。

legacy-celestial/cups-03.reason: 两名 Reviewer 都只辨出两个杯，但 reviewer-d 明确不能排除第三杯被遮，a 亦在不确定项承认可能完全遮挡；自身观察同样不能确认准确总数。因此拒绝强改为二杯，将所有现有三杯数量断言降级，并移除无法确认的新月对象条目。

judge.independentFinding: I opened the image first. At the lower left, below and beside the large glowing engraved star-chart disc, there is a group of three or four flat, layered, roughly rectangular forms catching a thin highlight along their top edges. At native resolution they carry no spines, no covers, no page-block striation and no binding — they read exactly as well as stacked stone slabs or low steps, and they sit continuous with the rock and roots around them. I cannot identify them as books. Two things I checked that the reviewers disputed and that I find the existing description gets RIGHT: (a) the object on the ground at the right genuinely is an armillary sphere on a stand — enlarged, it shows nested rings with an inner tilted ring read as an ellipse, radial meridian spokes, a protruding polar axis pin at the top, all mounted on a tiered stepped pedestal; (b) the disc in the upper right sky is a complete, unbroken circular sphere with faint surface mottling and no terminator line or crescent horns anywhere on it. Also confirmed and unchanged: three upright golden goblets standing in a row on the paving, a fourth goblet floating just above the open palm of a translucent nebula-hand reaching in from the right, and the seated figure's eyes open but directed down and to the viewer's left, away from the offered cup.

keyObjects: golden chalice held by the luminous hand
three golden chalices standing in a row on the ground
large gnarled tree trunk and branches
armillary sphere on a stand at the right
circular astrolabe or star chart leaning at the left
constellation lines and star points across the sky
small domed pavilion on the far shore

legacy-celestial/cups-04.reason: The books are the textbook MARK_UNCERTAIN case: the existing description asserts a specific identification that the pixels do not support, and I cannot substitute a confident alternative either — 'stone slabs' is no better evidenced than 'books'. Both reviewer-c and reviewer-e independently flagged it on the same grounds (no spines, covers, page edges or bindings; flat rectangles in deep shadow), and I independently agree after enlarging the region 12x. Because it is ambiguous rather than unambiguous, it fails AUTO_CORRECT threshold 1, so I remove the claim instead of rewriting it. I name the items rather than discarding the whole keyObjects field, so the reliable entries both reviewers confirmed — the chalices, the tree, the armillary sphere, the astrolabe disc, the constellation lines, the pavilion — all survive. Three items are named. The first is the books entry itself. The second is the self-reported-uncertainty line 'exact number of books in the left-hand stack', which presupposes the same unsupported identification and would otherwise be left dangling. The third is the self-reported-uncertainty line offering 'crescent moon' as a possibility: both reviewers independently and explicitly ruled out a crescent, and I confirmed the disc is a complete unbroken circle, so leaving that line in would feed the interpretation model an option that is affirmatively false. Dropping it costs almost nothing, since no moon phase is asserted as fact anywhere else in the record. I am overturning reviewer-e on the armillary sphere: reviewer-e claimed no vertical stand, no nested rings and no three-dimensional armature are resolvable, but all three are plainly visible when enlarged, and reviewer-c independently described it as a 'ring device on a post'. The existing keyObjects and spatialRelations entries for the armillary sphere are correct and are left untouched.

judge.independentFinding: I opened the image and zoomed the raised hand at 9x and at 16x nearest-neighbour. The figure stands back-to-viewer on a round tiered platform in water, viewer-right arm raised with index finger extended toward the wheel's lower rim node. Against the wheel's main graduated band there is a clear gap, but a thin hairline arc of the wheel and the wheel's vertical axis stem come down exactly to the fingertip. At native resolution the fingertip and that line are separated by at most one or two pixels, and the glow around the node bleeds over the finger, so I cannot establish whether there is contact or a small gap. The rest of the described scene checks out: four constellation line-figures (winged humanoid with an open book upper-left, winged bird upper-right, bull lower-left, lion lower-right), a large armillary sphere on the figure's viewer-left and a smaller ringed instrument plus a lit lantern on the viewer-right, warm horizon glow behind mountains, platform mirrored in the water.

visualTensions: the figure's small scale against the enormous ring
warm horizon glow against the cold blue-violet sky

legacy-celestial/major-10.reason: The existing visualTensions item asserts a definite separation ('almost but not quite'), and builds a tension on it. Reviewer-e flagged it and reviewer-f independently recorded in his blind observation that he 'cannot tell whether the raised fingertip makes contact with the wheel's rim or stops just short of it'; reviewer-b, although he voted pass, also recorded it non-committally as 'touching or nearly touching'. So the unresolvability is independently on record from more than one reviewer and matches my own zoom. I am NOT applying reviewer-e's patch: it swaps one unverifiable assertion (a gap) for the opposite unverifiable assertion (contact), which fails threshold 1 - the visual fact is ambiguous, not unambiguous. The correct action is to drop the over-asserted item rather than flip it. I am naming only the visualTensions item; the spatialRelations line 'its raised hand nearly touching the ring's lower rim' is a soft hedge compatible with either reading, so I am leaving it in to minimise loss.

judge.independentFinding: I opened the image and brightened/zoomed three regions before reading the packet. Mask: on the plinth sits a horned helm-like mask whose two almond eye apertures are distinctly LIGHTER than the near-black face around them, with a faint warm glow inside - they are the brightest thing on the mask and the reason it reads as the visual centre. 'Dark eye openings' inverts the actual tonal relationship. Figures: at 4x the left figure is unambiguously a full rear view - back of the head, shoulder line and the fall of the robe down his back, face not visible - with both arms raised overhead, each hand gripping a chain; the chain is unmistakably a chain, with individual oval links I can count, looped over his head and running down his back and left hip. His wrists are not shackled; his hands grip it freely. The right figure is also a rear view: her back is to us, her robe falls away from us, and only her head is turned in profile toward the viewer's left, toward the altar; her near hand is raised bare and open onto the chain lying on her shoulder. So neither torso is turned toward the mask.

replace.find: horned mask with two curved horns and dark eye openings
replace.with: horned mask with two curved horns and pale, luminous eye openings

replace.find: the two figures face inward toward the central mask, framing it symmetrically
replace.with: the two figures stand one on each side of the central mask, both seen from behind with their backs to the viewer; only the right figure's head is turned toward it

legacy-celestial/major-15.reason: I am patching only the two items that clear all five thresholds, and deliberately leaving the rest. (1) Mask eyes: visually unambiguous, reported independently by BOTH reviewer-b (high confidence) and reviewer-d (medium), confirmed by my own brightened zoom, a pure observable tonal fact, expressible as one exact substring swap. (2) 'face inward toward the central mask': both reviewers raised it independently, and both of their blind observations state without prompting that both figures are seen from behind with their backs to the viewer - reviewer-b 'bodies turned away from the viewer', reviewer-d 'both with their backs to the viewer'. I confirmed it myself. But the two reviewers then diverge on the SYMMETRY clause: reviewer-b wants to keep 'flanking the mask symmetrically', reviewer-d denies symmetry because the left figure stands markedly closer and renders larger. Since that part is contested and is a compositional judgement rather than an observable, my replacement encodes only the triply-confirmed facts (rear view, one on each side, the right figure's head turned toward the mask) and simply omits the symmetry claim rather than asserting or denying it. Not patched: reviewer-b's third issue, 'the chain arcs from the left figure's raised hands across the upper left of the frame'. Reviewer-d never raised it, so threshold 2 bars it outright, and on looking I find the claim only loosely imprecise rather than false - his raised hands genuinely do sit in the frame's upper-left region, even though the chain does not cross the open star field beyond him. That is a wording matter for a later pass, not a fact error. Both find strings were checked with grep -F against reveal/review-111.md; each occurs exactly once.

judge.independentFinding: Looking at the image myself before reading any reviewer: every object I can resolve in a figure's hands is the same flat, pale, open rectangular form held at chest height - the three figures at the bottom left, the hooded figure seated in the small boat at bottom right, and the waders scattered across the middle distance. Several of them glow faintly. I cannot find a single rolled, furled or spindled object anywhere in the frame. At this rendering size I also cannot positively confirm these are books or tablets rather than panels or lids - I can only confirm they are flat and open. Separately, I did see two ringed instruments on stands on the left platform, a larger multi-ring sphere and a smaller globe beside it, not one.

keyObjects: long horn with flared bell
stone tower platform with arched niches
armillary sphere on a stand
small lantern on the platform edge
large studded chest in the foreground
small rowing boat with a lantern
concentric ring lines in the sky

legacy-celestial/major-20.reason: The keyObjects entry asserts two object classes joined by 'and', and the second one ('scrolls') is a positive claim I cannot substantiate from the pixels. Reviewer-a affirmatively reports no rolled or furled form is resolvable anywhere; reviewer-c independently records in its uncertainObservations that 'whether the pale objects held are books, scrolls or lids is not resolvable at this size'. So the two reviewers do not jointly assert a replacement fact - one says the class is absent, the other says the class is undecidable - which fails the AUTO_CORRECT bar (no two-reviewer agreement on a single observable fact, and the fact is not unambiguous on the image). Dropping the item is the minimal-loss move: it removes an unverifiable object class rather than rewriting it into a different unverifiable one. I am naming the single item rather than the field, so the other seven keyObjects entries survive. The scene sentence repeats the same unverified word ('holding open tablets and scrolls') but I am not touching it, because dropping the whole scene line to remove two words would cost far more than it saves - flagging the keyObjects item is enough to stop the interpretation model from treating scrolls as established. On reviewer-c's separate armillary-sphere point I do NOT correct: both reviewers logged that count at only medium confidence, and more importantly 'armillary sphere on a stand' is an under-specified entry, not a false one - it never claims there is exactly one - so there is no factual error to fix.

judge.independentFinding: 棱面心由三剑穿入；人物坐看纸，桌另纸状物及暗小物，金属环仪和灯。左两浅圆盘类别/月相不稳。

large faceted crystal heart
open document held by the figure

legacy-celestial/swords-03.reason: f补two crescent moons无双人明确确认，Judge不确认，拒绝插入。a存疑红印，f声称蜡印，c无法辨认，Judge无法确认seal，过滤组合对象。

judge.independentFinding: Looking at the image myself first: the tall pointed arched window runs from the top of the artwork down to roughly the level of the reclining figure's head — about the upper half of the left edge. Below that point the left edge is solid interior: the armillary sphere on its tripod, the carved end panel of the stone bier, then polished dark floor carrying a large circular star-chart inlay. The window is simply not present along the lower half of the left edge. I also independently count three swords mounted point-down on the wall above the figure, evenly spaced with clear dark gaps, plus one separate blade laid horizontally along the front panel of the bier — these two groups are reliable. One figure lies supine, head left on a dark pillow, hands folded on the chest, covered by a constellation-patterned coverlet. A caged lantern with a warm flame stands at the right end. The wall is flat and covered in faint circular star-chart diagrams; no ceiling, vault rib or springing is visible anywhere in the frame, but the view is also cropped above the hanging blades, so I cannot affirm or deny a vault.

spatialRelations: the three wall swords hang above and to the right of the reclining figure
the caged lantern sits at the far right end of the slab, opposite the armillary sphere at the left
the floor star-map lies below and in front of the slab, centred under the composition

legacy-celestial/swords-04.reason: The 'full left edge' claim is wrong on the pixels — I verified that independently — but only ONE reviewer (reviewer-a, and only at medium confidence) raised it; reviewer-c did not. The two-reviewer threshold for AUTO_CORRECT is explicitly not met, so I will not rewrite it. Removing the single claim is the lower-cost, safer action than handing a false spatial assertion to the interpretation model, and it is excisable as one named list entry, so nothing else in spatialRelations is lost — the reliable entries (lantern opposite the armillary sphere, floor star-map below and in front of the slab, three swords above the figure) all survive. I did NOT action reviewer-c's separate objection to 'dark vaulted chamber' in the scene line: it too is single-reviewer, the ceiling is outside the crop so the claim is neither confirmable nor refutable from pixels, and 'vaulted' is a fragment inside the scene sentence rather than a list entry — excising it would require discarding the entire scene field, a cost far out of proportion to a low-impact architectural descriptor. The two reviewers do not contradict each other here; they each flagged a different unsupported assertion, so this is not a HUMAN_REVIEW case.

judge.independentFinding: Image-first: foreground figure holds point-down sword bundle; two swords lie on pavement; two distant figures face away. Cannot trace independent held hilt/guard/blade assemblies to verify exactly three. Border rules and side ticks visible, compass rosettes not resolved.

circular astrological floor engraving
Roman numeral V at top centre
text 'Five of Swords' at bottom
domed colonnaded structure at left
armillary sphere on a stand at left

legacy-celestial/swords-05.reason: Previous AUTO_PASS alleged reviewer-f placeholders/three cups, contradicted by current valid sword-scene evidence. Border correction has only one explicit reporter. Held count unresolved: a null, c three with two-or-four caveat, f confident three, Judge cannot verify. Filter repeated scene count and named object/motif claims; retain ground swords and other reliable evidence.

judge.independentFinding: Looking at the image myself first: there are two figures in the boat and they are not both seated. The farther figure STANDS upright - full torso, shoulders and head rise well clear of the gunwale, cloak falling in vertical folds to the boat's floor - with both hands high on a long pole/oar that angles down into the water off the boat's right side. Only the nearer figure, wrapped in a patterned blue-violet cloak, is seated. The boat is seen from astern: the end nearest me is the broad, rounded, carved transom, and the hull narrows away toward the far end; both figures face away from me toward the golden horizon glow, and the reflected light track runs from the horizon down the water toward the boat. So the bow points away, not toward the viewer. Upright blades line both rails - I read three to a side but could not rule out another hidden behind the standing figure's cloak.

replace.find: Two cloaked figures sit in a wooden rowboat on dark water, one rowing
replace.with: Two cloaked figures travel in a wooden rowboat on dark water, one seated and one standing at the oar

replace.find: the boat occupies the lower centre, its bow toward the viewer
replace.with: the boat occupies the lower centre, seen from astern, its bow pointing away toward the horizon

legacy-celestial/swords-06.reason: Both edits clear all five gates. Posture: reviewer-b and reviewer-d independently raised that one figure stands rather than sits, both at high confidence, and I saw it unaided - the standing/seated split is unmistakable in the silhouette. The existing file is also self-contradictory, since its own keyObjects line already says 'long wooden oar held by the standing figure' while the scene says both figures sit. Boat orientation: reviewer-b and reviewer-d again both raised it independently (medium and high), and I confirmed it myself from the carved transom nearest the viewer, the hull tapering away, and both figures facing the horizon glow. Both are observable facts - posture and orientation - not interpretation, and both express as exact substring replacements verified verbatim against reveal/review-317.md. I chose reviewer-d's framing over reviewer-b's for the scene line because reviewer-b's rewrite drops 'Two cloaked figures' from the opening, and the count of two is correct and worth keeping. I avoid the word 'poling': reviewer-d notes it cannot be determined whether the implement is a single oar or a punting pole, so I keep the neutral 'at the oar', which matches the existing keyObjects wording. I take no action on the blade count - both reviewers report six as a floor at only medium confidence, and the file's self-reported uncertainty already flags 'exact number of sword blades visible'.

judge.independentFinding: Looking at the image myself first: on the table at the left, two swords stand vertically, and both show an ornate cross-guard and ring pommel at the TOP with the blade narrowing downward into a short cylindrical socket at the table surface. Neither points skyward. The cloaked figure stands centre-right with its back to me, mid-stride toward the lit horizon on the right, carrying a tight bundle of blades against its right side with the hilts projecting above the shoulder. I could pick out roughly four distinct cross-guards at the top of that bundle but the shafts below overlap and merge into the dark cloak, so I cannot fix a total. I could NOT determine which way the head is facing - it is a dark silhouette against a dark sky.

replace.find: two upright swords standing point-up in cylindrical holders on a table
replace.with: two swords standing hilt-up, blades driven point-down into cylindrical holders on a table

legacy-celestial/swords-07.reason: All five gates are met for the table-sword orientation. (1) The fact is unambiguous on the image and I verified it myself before reading any reviewer. (2) Reviewer-c AND reviewer-e independently raised this exact item, both at high confidence - not one passing and one objecting. (3) I reached the same conclusion independently. (4) Orientation is a pure observable fact, not interpretation. (5) It expresses as one precise substring replacement, checked verbatim against reveal/review-316.md. I am deliberately NOT touching two other things the reviewers raised. First, the head direction in visualTensions: reviewer-c says the head turns right toward the lit horizon while reviewer-e says it turns back over the shoulder toward the table on the left - a direct contradiction - and I could not resolve it from the pixels either, so 'the figure's body faces away while the head turns back toward the camp' stays as-is and should be treated as unverified; it sits in visualTensions, a soft field, so leaving it costs less than acting on a coin-flip. Second, the carried-bundle count: both reviewers agree the total is unresolvable, but they disagree on how many hilts are separable (three vs four), so I will not write a replacement number - and the file's own self-reported uncertainty already flags that count, which limits the downstream damage.

judge.independentFinding: I opened the image before reading any reviewer notes. A barefoot woman in a dark star-flecked gown walks mid-stride TOWARD THE VIEWER down the open lane between two flanking ranks of swords on stone plinths; her body faces the viewer, her toes point toward the bottom of the frame, and the nearest swords are the largest in the frame. Both her hands are raised to the ends of a pale cloth band lying flat across her eyes; her head is bowed. The domed lit building is in the middle distance at roughly x=355 in a 560-wide frame, while the figure is at roughly x=265 and the open lane between the ranks is centred near x=280 - so the dome sits well RIGHT of the walkway's centre line, raised on a bank, its warm doorway throwing a gold reflection onto the water to the right. It is behind her, not ahead of her. I counted 8 swords, 4 per side, each on its own dark plinth. On every one the round ball pommel is at the very top, then the grip, then the crossguard, then the blade running DOWN into the plinth. The large body in the upper right is a cratered sphere encircled by a thin elliptical ring line.

replace.find: walks forward along a wet stone path between two rows of upright swords, lifting a pale cloth from her eyes, toward a small domed lit building under a star-filled sky
replace.with: walks forward toward the viewer along a wet stone path between two rows of upright swords, lifting a pale cloth from her eyes, with a small domed lit building on the rise behind her under a star-filled sky

replace.find: the domed building sits behind her, centred on the path's vanishing point
replace.with: the domed building sits behind her and well to the right of the walkway's centre line, raised on a bank above the water, its lit doorway reflected on the water

legacy-celestial/swords-08.reason: Two observable-fact corrections, both clearing the threshold. FIX 1 (direction of travel): the scene claims she walks 'toward a small domed lit building'. reviewer-d raised this formally at confidence=high, and reviewer-b independently recorded the same fact in his blind observation before comparison - spatialRelations: 'the figure walks forward toward the viewer, between the two flanking sword groups' and 'the lit building sits behind her right shoulder in the distance' - so the two-reviewer bar is met on the formal report plus blind-observation concordance. I verified it myself from the figure's facing, stride and the near-to-far sword scale. The reveal also self-contradicts: its own spatialRelations already says the dome 'sits behind her'. FIX 2 (dome position): both Reviewers raised this formally and in near-identical words - reviewer-b ('noticeably to the RIGHT of the walkway's centre line') and reviewer-d ('noticeably right of centre, on a rise beside the water, not on the path's centre line') - and both independently logged 'right of center' in their blind observations. I measured the offset myself. Position is an observable fact. Both replacements are exact substrings confirmed unique with grep -F. WHAT I DELIBERATELY DID NOT ACT ON: (a) SWORD ORIENTATION - reviewer-b says the swords are hilt-up/point-down into the plinth and wants 'upright swords' rewritten; reviewer-d's summary says the opposite ('every one points UP ... none inverted'). This is a direct Reviewer contradiction, but I can resolve it from the image and I agree with reviewer-b on the geometry: the ball pommel is plainly topmost, with the blade descending into the plinth. I still did not patch it, because the existing wording 'upright swords with round pommels and crossguards' does not actually assert point-up - 'upright' states that they stand vertically, which is true - so reviewer-b's objection is about the connotation of a word, and wording preference is never grounds for AUTO_CORRECT. Note also that reviewer-d's own component ordering ('round pommel at the very top, hilt below') agrees with reviewer-b and contradicts his own summary label, so his dissent is internally inconsistent rather than a genuine rival observation. (b) CLOTH MOTION - 'the cloth is being lifted rather than tied in place' (visualTensions) and 'the blindfold slipping away' (emphasizedAspects) assert a direction of motion that cannot be recovered from a still frame. Both Reviewers independently say so: reviewer-b formally ('direction of motion is not recoverable from the pixels') and reviewer-d in his blind uncertainObservations ('Whether the figure is pulling the cloth off her eyes or tying it on cannot be determined from a still image'). I agree - I cropped the head at 6x and both hands grip the band flat across the eye line, with no cue to direction. This is an unverifiable claim rather than a wrong one, so it belongs on the MARK_UNCERTAIN path, not inside a correction patch; since only one decision per card is allowed and the two positional errors are the higher-value fix, I left the motion wording untouched and kept 'lifting a pale cloth from her eyes' verbatim in my scene replacement rather than silently making an uncertainty call inside a correction. FLAGGING IT HERE for a follow-up uncertainty pass: the items to drop or neutralise are visualTensions 'the cloth is being lifted rather than tied in place' and emphasizedAspects 'the blindfold slipping away'. (c) SWORD COUNT - reviewer-b recorded null, reviewer-d and I both read 8 (4+4); the reveal asserts no number and already lists the count under self-reported uncertainty, so nothing needs changing. (d) 'ringed planet in the upper right sky' - neither Reviewer mentioned a ring and both described only a cratered disc, but I cropped it at 7x and a thin elliptical ring line does encircle the body, so the existing entry is correct and stands.

judge.independentFinding: I opened the image before reading any reviewer notes and zoomed the foreground at 6x. Ten swords stand on a circular engraved stone dais: five on the left arc, five on the right arc, each with an ornamented gold pommel and cross-guard at its TOP end and the blade tapering downward into a dark round socket cut into the floor. The orientation is identical on all ten. The dais's near rim is fully inside the frame (its front face and engraved band are visible, not cropped) and carries no swords; the far-centre gap, through which the cloaked figure is visible, carries none either. So the two groups of five face each other across the cloth rather than ringing it. The pale tan sheet is a torn parchment with ragged, lifted edges and drawn line-work, clearly sitting on top of the stone.

replace.find: ten upright swords set point-up in a ring of stone sockets
replace.with: ten upright swords set point-down into stone sockets, hilts and pommels uppermost

replace.find: the ring of swords encircles the fallen cloak and map in the lower half of the image
replace.with: two arcs of five swords flank the fallen cloak and map on the left and right of the platform, leaving the near and far edges of the circle open

legacy-celestial/swords-10.reason: Meets all five thresholds on two items. (1) Orientation: unambiguous at 6x on all ten blades; reviewer-c raised it as a high-confidence issue, and reviewer-a independently recorded 'blades set point-down into the stone... hilts and pommels catching light' in its own blind observation, so two reviewers report the same thing; I reached the same conclusion from the pixels myself; it is observable orientation, not interpretation; and it is a single precise substring. 'Point-up' is a straight inversion of what is painted. (2) Layout: reviewer-c flagged 'encircles' as wrong and reviewer-a independently described 'two symmetrical arcs... with a gap in the middle'; I verified the near rim is in frame and empty, so 'encircles' is a positional error, also fixable as one substring. I deliberately did NOT patch reviewer-a's 'broken column at right' plural complaint (completeness preference, reviewer-c could not count them either) nor reviewer-c's low-confidence doubts about the cloth and the parchment — at 5x the tan sheet shows torn edges and drawn markings, so the existing wording stands and reviewer-c is overturned there.

judge.independentFinding: On my first pass, before opening the packet, I noted the lanterns as sitting on the platform floor: one at lower left by the near post's base, one at centre beside the food spread, one at lower right. Each has a visible base resting on the inlaid stone and its own reflection in the wet surface. Zooming the post tops shows flower clusters, ribbons and tiny wound point-lights — nothing suspended from any post.

replace.find: small lanterns hanging on the posts
replace.with: small lanterns standing on the platform floor

legacy-celestial/wands-04.reason: Both reviewers independently returned 'corrected' on exactly this fact and described it identically (lanterns standing on the platform, nothing hanging from the posts); I reached the same conclusion on my own. It is a pure position fact, and the fix is two exact, uniquely-anchored substring swaps. Reviewer-e's separate 'ringed planet with orbiting spheres' point was raised by one reviewer only and is not included.
